question: What is the main function of phosphorus when it works together with calcium in the body?

options.A: They increase the speed of nerve impulses
options.B: They dissolve excess stomach acid
options.C: They prevent high blood pressure in the legs
options.D: They build and maintain strong bones and teeth

explanation: Calcium and phosphorus combine to form crystals that give structural strength to bones and teeth. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T7#BMP118_U2_T7_h2)

question: What key document must always go with a woman when transferring her from a PHC to a secondary hospital?

options.A: The original receipt for antenatal registration fees paid at the clinic
options.B: A personal letter of introduction written by the patient's husband
options.C: A signed consent form allowing surgical procedures at the tertiary center
options.D: A clear, written referral note detailing assessments and interventions

explanation: Receiving clinicians need to know what care has already been given and why the patient was transferred to act quickly. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h6)

question: What makes an inevitable abortion different from a threatened abortion?

options.A: The cervix remains completely closed and firm to the touch.
options.B: There is never any vaginal bleeding present during the episode.
options.C: The pregnancy process cannot be stopped and will not continue.
options.D: All products of conception have already passed out of the body.

explanation: An inevitable abortion means the changes in the cervix and uterus guarantee the pregnancy will end, unlike a threatened abortion where it might survive. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h1)

question: Where is the safest place to routine-check a newborn's temperature?

options.A: In the middle of the axilla
options.B: Inside the rectum
options.C: Against the forehead skin
options.D: Under the tongue

explanation: Axillary temperature measurement is safe, non-invasive, and reliable when done correctly in newborns. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T3#BMP220_U3_T3_h4)

question: Who usually assigns the official generic name to a new drug?

options.A: Patient advocacy groups in local communities
options.B: The local patent office in each individual state
options.C: International bodies like the World Health Organization
options.D: Private manufacturing companies seeking profit

explanation: Global organizations coordinate to give drugs clear, non-proprietary generic names that remain consistent worldwide. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T2#BMP124_U1_T2_h3)

question: What does a birth preparedness plan primarily help a pregnant woman avoid during an obstetric emergency?

options.A: Anxiety about the normal duration of labor
options.B: The need to undergo routine blood pressure checks
options.C: Dangerous delays in reaching a health facility
options.D: High costs of purchasing infant clothing items

explanation: Planning ahead for transport and funds prevents critical delays in accessing emergency care when complications arise. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h2)

question: What are the most common side effects reported by women using the Copper T 380A?

options.A: High blood pressure and severe headaches
options.B: Complete absence of all monthly bleeding
options.C: Heavier and more painful menstrual periods
options.D: Sudden hair loss and rapid weight gain

explanation: The local effect of copper and the device itself frequently leads to increased menstrual flow and cramping, particularly in the first few months. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T8#BMP224_U3_T8_h5)

question: A woman at 30 weeks gestation is having frequent contractions at a rural clinic. Why is salbutamol given to her?

options.A: To make sure she delivers her baby vaginally instead of by surgery
options.B: To permanently cure her risk of having another early labor
options.C: To help her placenta grow larger before the baby arrives
options.D: To delay birth long enough to transfer her to a better equipped hospital

explanation: Short-term tocolysis buys time to move a vulnerable mother and baby to a facility that can handle preterm newborns. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h3)

question: Besides the biological mother, who else can safely help provide skin-to-skin contact when the mother is tired?

options.A: Any adult visitor waiting in the corridor
options.B: Senior medical students on rotation
options.C: Trained hospital ward cleaners
options.D: Other family members like fathers or grandmothers

explanation: Family members such as fathers can share KMC duties to give the mother a chance to rest while keeping care continuous. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T4#BMP220_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is waiting for patients to come to the clinic often less effective than actively going into the community?

options.A: It requires more financial funding from the local government council
options.B: It fails to build local ownership and long-term trust in health programs
options.C: It causes immediate shortages of essential obstetric drugs in the clinic
options.D: It prevents midwives from administering routine immunizations to children

explanation: When people are involved in their own healthcare, they care more about the program and keep up healthy habits over time. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which finding is a sign of severe dehydration rather than some dehydration?

options.A: Lethargy or unconsciousness
options.B: Immediate skin recoil after pinching
options.C: Eager and greedy drinking behavior
options.D: Normal peripheral pulse volume

explanation: Lethargy, limpness, and reduced consciousness signal critical lack of blood flow to the brain, which occurs in severe dehydration. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T2#BMP222_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which hormone surge is linked to early pregnancy nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.B: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.C: Adrenocorticotropic hormone
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Rapidly rising human chorionic gonadotropin levels in the first trimester strongly correlate with nausea and vomiting. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is physical therapy used for a child recovering from paralytic polio?

options.A: To completely reverse the destruction of spinal cord motor neurons
options.B: To cure associated respiratory infections without using oxygen
options.C: To prevent permanent joint contractures and maintain muscle tone
options.D: To speed up the elimination of the live virus from the gut

explanation: While physical therapy cannot restore dead nerve cells, it keeps limbs flexible and prevents shortening of muscles and tendons. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T8#BMP222_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a category used to classify signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Theoretical signs
options.B: Positive signs
options.C: Presumptive signs
options.D: Probable signs

explanation: Pregnancy signs are strictly classified into presumptive, probable, and positive categories. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why are very watery, thin porridges not recommended as main meals for babies?

options.A: They cause immediate permanent damage to the infant kidneys
options.B: They contain too much protein for an immature liver to process
options.C: They are completely impossible for a human infant to swallow
options.D: They fill the baby's stomach quickly without providing enough energy and nutrients

explanation: Watery porridges have low energy density, meaning the baby fills up on water rather than the nutrients they need to grow. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is an advantage of asking open-ended questions during a counseling session?

options.A: They encourage clients to share more details about their concerns
options.B: They force the client to give a direct yes or no answer
options.C: They allow the midwife to finish the consultation much faster
options.D: They prevent the client from asking difficult medical questions

explanation: Open-ended questions prompt clients to explain their thoughts and feelings in their own words, revealing deeper insights into their reproductive needs. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T7#BMP126_U2_T7_h3)

question: What does an equal and active rooting response on both sides of the face tell the midwife?

options.A: The baby is definitely ready to be introduced to solid foods
options.B: The mother had an entirely uncomplicated pregnancy and birth
options.C: The lower motor pathways and brainstem are functioning normally
options.D: The infant has received all necessary routine childhood immunizations

explanation: Equal responses on both sides show that the relevant brainstem structures and nerve pathways are working well. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why are peer education programs often successful among teenagers?

options.A: Peer educators are licensed medical doctors and surgeons
options.B: Teenagers prefer lectures delivered by elderly community leaders
options.C: Peer educators never require any training or supervision
options.D: Young people relate better to peers who share their experiences

explanation: Adolescents open up more easily to individuals close to their own age who understand their daily social pressures and language. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is clear communication essential for a ward manager in a busy maternity unit?

options.A: It prevents midwives from taking any annual leave days
options.B: It eliminates the need for any written nursing documentation
options.C: It bridges hospital policies with safe bedside care delivery
options.D: It ensures doctors never have to speak directly with patients

explanation: Good communication ensures that management goals are properly understood and carried out by the clinical team looking after mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T1#BMP312_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why are newborns at a much higher risk of hospital-acquired infections during procedures?

options.A: Excessive body fat distribution
options.B: Immature immune system response
options.C: Rapid metabolic clearance rates
options.D: High baseline red blood cell count

explanation: Newborns, especially preterm babies, do not yet have fully developed immune systems to fight off germs easily. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T1#BMP220_U3_T1_h6)

question: At which grade of uterine prolapse does the cervix descend all the way to the level of the vaginal opening?

options.A: Fourth-degree
options.B: Zero-degree
options.C: Second-degree
options.D: First-degree

explanation: Second-degree prolapse means the cervix has dropped down to the level of the introitus or vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h4)

question: What does the term hepatitis mean?

options.A: Failure of the gallbladder
options.B: Inflammation of the liver
options.C: Swelling of the kidneys
options.D: Infection of the placenta

explanation: Hepatitis simply means inflammation of the liver tissue, which can be caused by viruses or other factors. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why must the school nurse actively involve parents and guardians in the school health program?

options.A: To teach parents how to diagnose complex medical conditions
options.B: To force parents to take over the daily nursing duties in the clinic
options.C: To ensure health habits and hygiene practices are reinforced at home
options.D: To collect extra financial donations for buying sports equipment

explanation: Health education is most effective when messages taught at school are supported and practiced consistently at home by family members. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T5#BMP126_U3_T5_h8)

question: You check a newborn boy and notice his testes are down in a folded scrotum. What does this mean?

options.A: It is an abnormal swelling caused by birth trauma.
options.B: It suggests the baby was actually born prematurely.
options.C: It is a normal, expected finding for a term male newborn.
options.D: It indicates an endocrine disorder requiring immediate surgery.

explanation: Descended testes and a wrinkled scrotum are signs of a full-term baby boy. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T2#BMP214_U1_T2_h2)

question: How do tight synthetic clothes and non-breathable underwear contribute to repeat yeast infections?

options.A: Synthetic fibers release toxic chemicals that directly stimulate fungal spore production.
options.B: They trap heat and moisture in the vulvar area, creating an ideal environment for fungi to multiply.
options.C: They prevent the natural blood supply from reaching the external genitalia.
options.D: They physically scrape the vaginal walls and cause bleeding that attracts fungi.

explanation: Fungi thrive in warm, dark, and humid conditions, which are easily created by tight synthetic garments that block air circulation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h7)

question: What public health intervention is most effective in preventing several severe childhood infections that disrupt growth?

options.A: Routine childhood immunization
options.B: Enforced bed rest during the rainy season
options.C: Exclusive use of bottled mineral water
options.D: Daily administration of multivitamins

explanation: Vaccines protect children from debilitating diseases like measles and polio that impair growth. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T2#BMP222_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why is mumps able to spread before anyone even notices the child is sick?

options.A: Antibiotics activate the dormant viral particles
options.B: The rash is invisible during the first week
options.C: The virus sheds into the air days before swelling starts
options.D: Children hide their symptoms from their parents

explanation: Infectious viral particles are released into respiratory secretions before physical signs like parotid swelling become visible, driving community spread. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T2#BMP222_U2_T2_h2)

question: At approximately what age should a healthy child be able to walk independently?

options.A: Eighteen to twenty-four months
options.B: Two to four months
options.C: Six to eight months
options.D: Twelve to fifteen months

explanation: Most toddlers take their first independent steps around their first birthday, up to about 15 months. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T1#BMP222_U1_T1_h3)

question: What pattern seen under a microscope confirms the presence of amniotic fluid in a fern test?

options.A: Long, thread-like fungal strands
options.B: Circular clusters of red blood cells
options.C: Clusters of oval skin cells
options.D: Crystals that look like fern leaves

explanation: When amniotic fluid dries on a glass slide, the high salt content forms a distinct fern leaf pattern under the microscope. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main idea behind supportive supervision instead of traditional inspection?

options.A: Reducing contact hours between staff and supervisors
options.B: Focusing solely on punishing poor record keeping
options.C: Joint problem-solving and continuous capacity building
options.D: Imposing strict financial penalties for minor errors

explanation: Supportive supervision treats mistakes as learning opportunities and builds the confidence and skills of community health workers through mentorship. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T1#BMP316_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is a midwifery perspective particularly valuable in modern occupational health settings?

options.A: It lowers the cost of medical insurance for large companies
options.B: It replaces the need for standard industrial safety engineers
options.C: It focuses exclusively on treating high-risk manufacturing injuries
options.D: It addresses the needs of women of childbearing age at work

explanation: Midwives understand female reproductive physiology and maternal needs, making them well-suited to protect female workers from workplace hazards. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T4#BMP126_U4_T4_h1)

question: Who are the key local leaders a midwife should talk to first when starting health outreach in a new community?

options.A: Foreign aid organization directors
options.B: Primary school football coaches
options.C: Federal ministry of health permanent secretaries
options.D: Traditional chiefs and religious leaders

explanation: Community gatekeepers like chiefs and religious leaders hold significant influence, and gaining their approval helps build trust with residents. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T2#BMP227_U2_T2_h1)

question: A woman develops a fast-growing, very painful vulvar hematoma two hours after birth. What is the usual first step in management?

options.A: Applying continuous warm compresses for forty-eight hours
options.B: Surgical evacuation of clots and ligation of the bleeding vessel
options.C: Administering high-dose oral iron supplements immediately
options.D: Packing the vagina tightly with dry gauze without anesthesia

explanation: Large or growing hematomas need to be opened, the trapped clots removed, and the bleeding vessel tied off. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T4#BMP311_U4_T4_h6)

question: What physical sign is commonly seen on infected tonsils?

options.A: Small black spots and bleeding ulcers
options.B: Clear fluid-filled blisters only
options.C: Complete absence of visible tissue
options.D: Patchy white exudates and redness

explanation: Inflamed tonsils typically show marked redness and pus-like white or yellow spots on their surface. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T2#BMP125_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a major danger of performing a blind finger sweep to clear a blocked airway?

options.A: Spreading an infection to the rescuer's fingers
options.B: Scratching the patient's tongue and causing mild pain
options.C: Pushing the foreign object deeper into the throat
options.D: Breaking the patient's lower teeth

explanation: Blind finger sweeps can easily wedge a loose object further down the windpipe, worsening the obstruction. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T2#BMP110_U7_T2_h5)

question: Which two ducts join together to form the common bile duct?

options.A: Main pancreatic duct and accessory duct
options.B: Right and left hepatic ducts
options.C: Esophageal duct and gastric duct
options.D: Cystic duct and common hepatic duct

explanation: The cystic duct from the gallbladder merges with the common hepatic duct draining the liver to create the common bile duct. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which symptom is most typical of gonococcal cervicitis in women?

options.A: Hard painless ulcer on the vulva
options.B: Lower abdominal rash with small fluid blisters
options.C: Intense itching with thick white cheese discharge
options.D: Purulent yellowish vaginal discharge

explanation: Gonococcal infection causes localized inflammation with a characteristic pus-filled cervical discharge. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a practical tool for handling sudden problems during fieldwork?

options.A: Having a pre-approved contingency plan
options.B: Canceling the entire study permanently
options.C: Ignoring safety rules to finish work faster
options.D: Blaming local participants for the delays

explanation: Contingency plans provide alternative strategies when unexpected obstacles like bad weather or transport breakdowns occur in the field. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T4#BMP225_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which medication works by helping blood to clot, directly reducing heavy menstrual flow?

options.A: Progesterone cream
options.B: Combined estrogen pills
options.C: Ibuprofen tablets
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic medicine. It stabilizes blood clots in the vessels of the uterus to slow down bleeding. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which trematode group is unique for having separate male and female sexes?

options.A: Liver flukes
options.B: Schistosomes
options.C: Intestinal flukes
options.D: Lung flukes

explanation: Unlike most other trematodes which are hermaphrodites, blood flukes or schistosomes exist as distinct male and female worms. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T9#BMP116_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which part of the nervous system triggers the relaxation of penile blood vessels to produce an erection?

options.A: Somatic motor system
options.B: Sympathetic nervous system
options.C: Enteric nervous system
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Parasympathetic nerve signals cause blood vessels in the erectile tissue to widen, allowing blood to fill the chambers. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which group of professionals forms the core multidisciplinary team for managing perinatal bipolar disorder?

options.A: Pharmacists, laboratory scientists, and opticians
options.B: Pediatricians, dietitians, and accountants
options.C: Surgeons, physiotherapists, and dentists
options.D: Midwives, obstetricians, and psychiatrists

explanation: Managing mental health during pregnancy requires close collaboration between maternity staff and mental health experts. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the phase called when fresh dialysate fluid sits inside the abdomen to filter waste products?

options.A: Infill phase
options.B: Flush phase
options.C: Dwell phase
options.D: Drain phase

explanation: The dwell phase is the resting period during which waste products and excess fluids cross the peritoneal membrane into the dialysate. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T9#BMP216_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the single most effective action a midwife takes to prevent the spread of infection during a home visit?

options.A: Closing all windows in the room
options.B: Wearing heavy rubber boots
options.C: Sprinkling disinfectant on the floor
options.D: Performing thorough hand hygiene

explanation: Washing hands with soap and water or using hand sanitizer stops the transmission of microorganisms between clients and the midwife. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T3#BMP215_U1_T3_h3)

question: A booking antenatal patient at 10 weeks gestation has a hemoglobin level of 10.2 g/dL. How should the midwife interpret this?

options.A: Normal, because pregnant women always have low blood counts
options.B: Anemic, because it is below the first trimester threshold
options.C: Normal, because hemodilution is already at its maximum
options.D: Critical, requiring an immediate blood transfusion

explanation: The first trimester threshold is 11.0 g/dL, so a reading of 10.2 g/dL falls below normal and indicates true anemia early in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T1#BMP221_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which layer of the endometrium is completely shed during menstruation?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Stratum basalis
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Stratum functionalis

explanation: The superficial stratum functionalis breaks down and sloughs off every month when hormone levels drop, while the deeper layer stays behind. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T5#BMP210_U2_T5_h2)

question: What does the pancreas do when a person develops severe insulin resistance?

options.A: It stops making digestive enzymes.
options.B: It produces extra insulin to overcome the resistance.
options.C: It turns stored fat into muscle.
options.D: It shrinks from lack of use.

explanation: To compensate for cells ignoring insulin, the pancreas works harder and secretes higher volumes of insulin into the blood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h2)

question: What should a midwifery school do when multiple students consistently fail a specific clinical skill assessment?

options.A: Blame the external regulatory body for the examination questions
options.B: Review and revise the curriculum, lesson plans, and teaching methods
options.C: Remove all practical assessments from the programme permanently
options.D: Assume the students are simply lazy and increase the passing mark

explanation: Widespread failure often signals a gap in how the material is taught or structured, requiring educators to evaluate and improve their own instruction. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h6)

question: How do computer hardware and software depend on each other to function?

options.A: Software provides physical power while hardware stores the digital files
options.B: Hardware is only used for typing while software is used exclusively for printing
options.C: Software and hardware operate completely independently without any connection
options.D: Hardware needs software to run instructions, and software needs hardware to execute them

explanation: The physical machine needs programs to know what to do, and those programs need a physical home to run on. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of performing a bimanual examination before inserting a copper IUCD?

options.A: To open the cervical canal without using any instruments
options.B: To clean away all bacteria surrounding the vaginal walls
options.C: To determine the size and position of the uterus
options.D: To measure the exact amount of copper needed in the womb

explanation: The bimanual exam allows the midwife to check the position of the uterus, helping ensure safe insertion. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T11#BMP224_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an informal community structure?

options.A: The federal ministry of health policy planning committee
options.B: Registered local government administrative offices
options.C: Traditional birth attendants and market women unions
options.D: State-funded primary health care board headquarters

explanation: Informal structures arise naturally from social ties and traditional practices rather than official government registration. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T1#BMP117_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which blood test result specifically points to a recent, acute rubella infection?

options.A: Elevated blood urea nitrogen
options.B: High white blood cell count only
options.C: Presence of rubella IgM antibodies
options.D: Absence of all immune cells

explanation: IgM antibodies appear in the blood soon after a primary infection, making them the standard marker for recent exposure. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T3#BMP222_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for placenta accreta in later pregnancies?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Mild pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: History of heavy morning sickness
options.D: Previous Caesarean section

explanation: Scars from prior uterine surgeries create sites where the placenta can grow straight into the muscle wall. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why do cephalosporins destroy bacteria without harming human maternal and fetal cells?

options.A: Maternal blood cells neutralize the drug before it reaches tissues
options.B: Human cells lack the peptidoglycan cell wall targeted by these drugs
options.C: Human cells actively digest the antibiotic molecules on contact
options.D: The placenta creates an impenetrable shield against beta-lactams

explanation: Human cells have flexible membranes instead of the rigid peptidoglycan cell walls that cephalosporins target, keeping human cells safe. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T3#BMP124_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why are arm restraints sometimes used right after a baby has surgery for a cleft lip?

options.A: To make it easier for nurses to check the intravenous cannula
options.B: To stop the infant from rolling off the hospital bed
options.C: To keep the baby lying completely flat during sleep hours
options.D: To prevent the infant from scratching or disturbing the surgical suture line

explanation: Babies naturally reach for their faces, so gentle arm restraints keep their hands away from the fresh stitches while healing. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T5#BMP220_U2_T5_h6)

question: What primary practice by patients contributes most to the rise of drug-resistant malaria parasites?

options.A: Sleeping under insecticide-treated bed nets every night
options.B: Stopping treatment early when symptoms start to fade
options.C: Washing malaria tablets down with clean drinking water
options.D: Attending antenatal clinics regularly for checkups

explanation: Stopping medication early leaves the strongest parasites alive in the body, allowing them to multiply and develop resistance to the drug. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T12#BMP124_U4_T12_h6)

question: How long do current guidelines recommend waiting before giving a newborn their first bath?

options.A: Only 30 minutes
options.B: At least 24 hours
options.C: Exactly 2 hours
options.D: Up to one week

explanation: Delaying the bath for at least 24 hours helps stabilize the baby's temperature and blood sugar. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T5#BMP214_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is one of the respiratory functions of the scalene muscles?

options.A: Elevating the upper ribs during forced breathing
options.B: Contracting the diaphragm downward
options.C: Expanding the abdominal cavity
options.D: Pushing air out of the stomach

explanation: By attaching to the first and second ribs, the scalenes help lift the ribcage during deep or labored breathing. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the very first step in managing an emergency case of heavy bleeding from an inevitable abortion?

options.A: Assess airway, breathing, and circulation for stability.
options.B: Perform a detailed pelvic ultrasound scan immediately.
options.C: Administer oral iron supplements to prevent future anemia.
options.D: Send the patient home to rest until the bleeding stops.

explanation: Emergency care always starts with the primary survey checking vital life signs: airway, breathing, and circulation. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h5)

question: A child has a mild fever and a pink rash that started on the face and spread to the body. About how long does the typical rubella rash last before clearing up?

options.A: About 2 weeks
options.B: In a few hours
options.C: Next month
options.D: About 3 days

explanation: The rubella rash is short-lived, usually clearing up within about three days of its onset. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T3#BMP222_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is a midwife checking for when assessing Goodell sign?

options.A: Bluish color of the vagina
options.B: Compressibility of the lower uterus
options.C: Enlargement of the abdomen
options.D: Softening of the cervix

explanation: Goodell sign refers specifically to the softening of the cervical tissue resulting from increased vascularity and fluid retention. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T2#BMP212_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which delay in the three delays model does an emergency maternal transport scheme directly address?

options.A: The delay in diagnosing pregnancy complications
options.B: The delay in receiving treatment at the hospital
options.C: The delay in reaching a health facility
options.D: The delay in deciding to seek care

explanation: Transport schemes focus entirely on moving the patient physically from the community to a referral center, solving the second delay. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is a previous classical uterine scar considered an absolute contraindication for oxytocin induction?

options.A: It increases the risk of complete uterine rupture during strong contractions
options.B: It stops the placenta from attaching properly to the uterine wall
options.C: It guarantees that the baby will be born prematurely
options.D: It prevents the pituitary gland from releasing natural hormones

explanation: A classical scar runs vertically through the thick upper segment of the uterus, making it dangerously weak and prone to tearing under induced contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T1#BMP213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of physiological jaundice?

options.A: Normal feeding and active behavior
options.B: Gradual daily rise in bilirubin levels
options.C: Appearance within the first 12 hours of life
options.D: Resolution within two weeks of birth

explanation: Appearance within the first 12 hours is extremely early and classifies the jaundice as pathological, not physiological. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T6#BMP220_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does the practice of open disclosure primarily involve?

options.A: Handing over all personal staff files to the patient's relatives
options.B: Refusing to speak with relatives until an official lawyer arrives
options.C: Transparent and honest communication with families after an adverse event
options.D: Publicly posting hospital error statistics on social media networks

explanation: Open disclosure ensures families receive truthful, empathetic information regarding unexpected complications during maternity care. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to use both a patient card and a clinic register during mobile outreach?

options.A: It gives the midwife something boring to do while waiting for patients to arrive
options.B: It allows the government to tax pregnant women based on their clinic attendance
options.C: It prevents loss of critical health data if the patient card gets misplaced or damaged
options.D: It ensures that doctors in the city never have to speak with community midwives

explanation: Keeping records in both places ensures that even if a woman loses her card, her health history remains safely logged in the clinic register. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T2#BMP215_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why does full milk production usually wait until after pregnancy?

options.A: The infant has not yet stimulated the neural receptors
options.B: High levels of estrogen and progesterone block milk production
options.C: The alveoli are not yet fully formed until labor starts
options.D: Oxytocin levels are too high to allow synthesis

explanation: During pregnancy, high levels of placenta hormones keep milk production on hold until the placenta is delivered. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T1#BMP214_U3_T1_h1)

question: When is bromocriptine therapy usually started after birth to suppress milk production?

options.A: Within the first few hours or days postpartum
options.B: At the first sign of infant weaning
options.C: Only when breast abscesses begin to form
options.D: After six weeks of exclusive breastfeeding

explanation: The medication is most effective when given early, before the mother's milk supply becomes fully established. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T7#BMP213_U4_T7_h3)

question: A client requests a tubal ligation because her husband is forcing her to do it. What is your best action as the midwife?

options.A: Book the surgery immediately to satisfy the demands of the spouse
options.B: Provide private counseling to ensure the decision is truly voluntary by the client
options.C: Perform the procedure quietly without documenting the husband's involvement
options.D: Refuse service entirely and report the couple to local community leaders

explanation: Informed consent requires that the choice is entirely voluntary and free from coercion by anyone, including a spouse. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h2)

question: What does a confounding variable do in an observational study?

options.A: It automatically cures every patient enrolled in the trial
options.B: It distorts the true relationship between the exposure and the outcome
options.C: It replaces the need for statistical tests in the final report
options.D: It speeds up data collection so the study finishes early

explanation: A confounder is an extra factor associated with both the exposure and the outcome, making it look like a direct link exists when it might be false. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T3#BMP225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What does the term 'potency' mean in pharmacology?

options.A: The speed at which a drug is cleared from blood
options.B: The tendency of a drug to cause adverse reactions
options.C: The maximum possible effect a drug can produce
options.D: The amount of drug needed to produce a specific effect

explanation: Potency measures the dose concentration required to achieve a desired biological response. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T5#BMP124_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is allowed during exclusive breastfeeding?

options.A: Prescribed medical drops
options.B: Diluted fruit juice
options.C: Herbal gripe water
options.D: Plain clean water

explanation: Vitamins, mineral supplements, or medicines prescribed by a clinician are allowed, but no water or other liquids. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main job of thrombin during the common clotting pathway?

options.A: To dissolve the platelet plug completely
options.B: To produce more red blood cells in bone marrow
options.C: To convert fibrinogen into fibrin strands
options.D: To destroy excess calcium ions in the blood

explanation: Thrombin acts as an enzyme that changes soluble fibrinogen into solid fibrin threads to build the clot. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a primary data source in a maternity ward?

options.A: The national budget allocation letter
options.B: The hospital generator maintenance log
options.C: The labor and delivery register
options.D: The annual medical journal subscription

explanation: Registers where patient encounters are first recorded serve as the fundamental source documents for HMIS. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T1#BMP123_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which physical sign is most characteristic of mumps?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eyes
options.B: A widespread itchy red skin rash
options.C: Painful swelling of the parotid glands
options.D: Stiffening of the neck muscles

explanation: Parotitis, or inflammation of the salivary glands near the jaw and ears, gives mumps its classic facial appearance. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T2#BMP222_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is cord prolapse a major danger when the membranes rupture in a transverse lie?

options.A: The placenta detaches prematurely from the upper uterine wall
options.B: The loose fit of the presenting part allows the cord to slip past
options.C: Uterine contractions squeeze the umbilical cord against the spine
options.D: Excessive amniotic fluid washes the fetus completely out

explanation: Because the shoulder does not plug the pelvis snugly like a head, the cord easily washes down when the water breaks. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T6#BMP311_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of trauma-informed care in clinical practice?

options.A: Focusing solely on immediate surgical repair of physical wounds
options.B: Understanding what happened to the patient to avoid re-traumatization
options.C: Ensuring the patient follows every hospital rule without question
options.D: Convincing the patient to press legal charges immediately

explanation: Trauma-informed care centers on understanding past trauma to prevent clinical procedures or interactions from triggering further distress. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is a missed period (amenorrhea) alone not a guaranteed sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Menstruation always stops abruptly during menopause
options.B: Stress and hormone imbalances can also stop menstrual periods
options.C: Implantation bleeding replaces a normal period entirely
options.D: Every pregnant woman continues to bleed monthly

explanation: Many non-pregnancy factors like emotional stress, weight changes, and illness can cause a missed period. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why does the baby's head make another visible turn (external rotation) shortly after birth?

options.A: Maternal pushing forces the neck muscles to contract.
options.B: The midwife turns the head to prevent shoulder dystocia.
options.C: The shoulders rotate internally inside the pelvis to fit the outlet.
options.D: The baby turns its face to breathe fresh air after birth.

explanation: As the shoulders inside the pelvis turn to line up for delivery, that internal movement makes the head outside turn along with them. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T4#BMP212_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which domain of learning involves the development of physical coordination and clinical procedures?

options.A: The cognitive domain
options.B: The reflective domain
options.C: The psychomotor domain
options.D: The affective domain

explanation: The psychomotor domain specifically deals with physical skills and hands-on clinical procedures like performing deliveries or giving injections. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T1#BMP312_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is an obstetric cause of asphyxia?

options.A: Carbon monoxide poisoning
options.B: Umbilical cord prolapse
options.C: Peanut aspiration
options.D: Smoke inhalation

explanation: Cord prolapse compresses the blood vessels supplying the fetus, cutting off oxygen delivery during labor. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T2#BMP110_U7_T2_h2)

question: Why is spotting mild chronic kidney disease important for women of childbearing age?

options.A: Kidney disease prevents women from ever getting pregnant
options.B: Pregnant women always require immediate dialysis
options.C: Mild kidney disease automatically causes twin pregnancies
options.D: Pregnancy can unmask or worsen underlying kidney problems

explanation: The extra blood volume and workload during pregnancy place added stress on the kidneys, which can reveal or speed up hidden renal issues. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T7#BMP216_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of involving youth advisory boards in clinic planning?

options.A: They replace trained midwives during night shifts
options.B: They prescribe medications during emergencies
options.C: They identify barriers adults might overlook
options.D: They manage the hospital financial budget

explanation: Working with youth gives clinics direct insight into adolescent preferences and obstacles that older planners might miss. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T5#BMP320_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which intervention serves as both a psychological calming tool and a physical pain-management strategy during labor?

options.A: Prolonged bed rest in isolation
options.B: High-dose intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Strict fluid restriction protocols
options.D: Controlled breathing exercises

explanation: Breathing techniques help calm the mind psychologically while relaxing tense muscles to cope with labor contractions physically. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T6#BMP223_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which blood vessel is most commonly catheterized to perform an exchange transfusion in a newborn?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Femoral artery
options.C: Jugular vein
options.D: Radial vein

explanation: The umbilical vein remains open for a short period after birth, making it the safest and most direct route for exchange procedures. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T7#BMP220_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do midwives in low-resource clinics sometimes perform a New Ballard Score on a newborn?

options.A: To check if the baby has received all routine immunizations
options.B: To estimate gestational age when the mother's menstrual dates are unknown
options.C: To test the infant's blood glucose levels after a long labor
options.D: To measure the exact birth weight of an extremely small baby

explanation: Physical and neurological signs assessed in the newborn score help estimate how many weeks old the baby is when accurate pregnancy history is missing. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of the oily secretions from the Montgomery glands on the areola?

options.A: Anchoring the baby's tongue during a feed
options.B: Lubricating and protecting the nipple
options.C: Providing extra protein to the baby
options.D: Stimulating the infant's rooting reflex

explanation: The Montgomery glands secrete a protective substance that keeps the nipple skin healthy and guards against cracking during frequent feeds. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary setting for care in domiciliary midwifery practice?

options.A: A primary health care clinic
options.B: The private home of the woman
options.C: A specialized maternity center
options.D: A tertiary teaching hospital

explanation: Domiciliary midwifery specifically refers to providing professional midwifery care inside the client's own residence rather than in a formal health facility. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T1#BMP215_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which chemical substance released by the endometrium is the primary cause of pain in primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prostaglandins
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Excessive prostaglandin production causes the uterus to contract strongly, reducing blood flow and resulting in crampy pain. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following bones forms the broad, upper fan-shaped part of the hip?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Coccyx
options.C: Pubis
options.D: Ischium

explanation: The ilium is the largest component of the coxal bone, creating the broad wing-like structure at the top. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T12#BMP111_U2_T12_h2)

question: What are parents most likely to feel right after learning their newborn has a facial cleft?

options.A: Excitement for early discharge
options.B: Immediate relief and joy
options.C: Indifference and apathy
options.D: Shock, grief, and anxiety

explanation: Finding out about an unexpected birth defect often brings up strong emotions and a natural grieving process for parents. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T5#BMP220_U2_T5_h5)

question: How do most Traditional Birth Attendants learn their maternity care skills?

options.A: Through online international certification courses
options.B: Through mandatory government medical postings
options.C: Through formal university nursing degrees
options.D: Through apprenticeships or family lineage

explanation: TBAs generally learn informally by working closely with older, experienced practitioners or through family traditions rather than through classroom medical education. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T1#BMP215_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which chamber of the heart suffers the most strain when pulmonary vascular resistance remains chronically high?

options.A: Left atrium
options.B: Sinoatrial node
options.C: Left ventricle
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: High resistance in the lungs forces the right ventricle to pump harder against high pressure, which can lead to right heart failure or cor pulmonale. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h6)

question: What does the term orthopnea mean when checking on a pregnant cardiac patient?

options.A: Shortness of breath that worsens when lying flat
options.B: Fainting spells occurring immediately after eating
options.C: Chest pain triggered exclusively by cold weather
options.D: Sudden swelling of the face and upper eyelids

explanation: Orthopnea means breathing gets harder when lying down, so patients often need extra pillows at night to ease fluid congestion. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T4#BMP221_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of fetal heart auscultation during labor?

options.A: To determine the exact gestational age
options.B: To confirm the presence of twin pregnancy
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the baby
options.D: To detect early signs of fetal distress

explanation: Listening to the fetal heart allows midwives to spot potential oxygen shortages early so they can act quickly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h1)

question: What systemic symptom frequently accompanies the local breast pain and redness in mastitis?

options.A: Sudden weight loss
options.B: Persistent dry cough
options.C: Swollen lower limbs
options.D: Fever and chills

explanation: Systemic inflammatory responses to the infection often cause flu-like symptoms, including a high temperature and shaking chills. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important for a midwife to note how a patient's temperature was measured?

options.A: Different body sites give slightly different baseline temperature readings.
options.B: Armpit readings are always higher than internal core values.
options.C: The brain only responds to temperatures taken in the ear.
options.D: Only oral thermometers can detect hypothermia.

explanation: Sites like the mouth, ear, and armpit measure temperature a little differently, so clinicians account for these variations during assessment. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T5#BMP111_U4_T5_h5)

question: When is ECT typically considered for a patient with a mental health condition?

options.A: Before trying any talk therapy or medication
options.B: When other standard treatments have failed
options.C: Only when the patient requests outpatient therapy
options.D: As the very first step in routine counseling

explanation: Medical teams usually reserve ECT for severe cases where medications and talk therapy have not provided relief. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T5#BMP223_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the term for passing Hepatitis B from a mother to her baby during childbirth?

options.A: Airborne transmission
options.B: Horizontal transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Vertical transmission

explanation: Vertical transmission means passing an infection from a mother to her child during pregnancy or delivery. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T7#BMP221_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why is male partner involvement particularly valuable when counseling couples on the TwoDay Method?

options.A: Partners pay for the laboratory tests required for charting
options.B: Partners are required to physically check the cervical secretions
options.C: Men must calculate the exact day of ovulation for the woman
options.D: Couples must mutually agree on periods of abstinence during fertile days

explanation: Because natural family planning relies on abstaining from unprotected intercourse during fertile days, cooperation and communication between both partners are essential. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T2#BMP224_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which sign shows that a baby is physically ready for solid foods?

options.A: Erupting the first permanent molar tooth
options.B: Holding the head steady and sitting upright
options.C: Showing complete refusal of all liquids
options.D: Walking a few steps with minimal support

explanation: Good head control and the ability to sit up help babies swallow safely and prevent choking. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the timeline for ophthalmia neonatorum in a newborn?

options.A: Any eye infection diagnosed during the antenatal period
options.B: Eye discharge appearing after the first six weeks
options.C: Chronic viral keratitis seen in older toddlers
options.D: Conjunctivitis occurring within the first 28 days of life

explanation: Ophthalmia neonatorum refers to any conjunctivitis that develops during the neonatal period, which is the first 28 days of life. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T2#BMP220_U2_T2_h1)

question: A client comes to the clinic 96 hours after unprotected sex asking for emergency contraception. What is the best action for the midwife?

options.A: Wait for her next menstrual period before offering any intervention
options.B: Offer a copper IUCD because she is still within the five-day window
options.C: Tell her it is too late for any emergency contraceptive method
options.D: Refuse the IUCD and give her high-dose progestin pills instead

explanation: Since 96 hours is within the 120-hour limit, a copper IUCD is a valid and effective option. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T11#BMP224_U3_T11_h2)

question: An infant with an ileostomy has a fluid loss of 15 mL over a four-hour nursing shift. How should this loss be managed?

options.A: Replace the 15 mL volume-for-volume with an appropriate fluid
options.B: Restrict total daily maintenance fluids by double that amount
options.C: Give a rapid injection of concentrated potassium chloride
options.D: Ignore the loss because minor bowel outputs do not affect neonates

explanation: Measured ongoing losses must be replaced milliliter for milliliter to keep blood pressure and electrolyte balance stable. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T5#BMP220_U3_T5_h4)

question: A nurse places an agitated patient in continuous seclusion for three days without documenting reasons or notifying a doctor. What legal risk does this nurse face?

options.A: An immediate promotion for maintaining strict ward discipline
options.B: Liability for unlawful detention and professional misconduct charges
options.C: A commendation from the Mental Health Review Tribunal
options.D: No risk at all, because nurses have absolute immunity in hospitals

explanation: Misusing seclusion without documentation or medical oversight violates the law and exposes the nurse to severe legal and professional penalties. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T3#BMP223_U1_T3_h7)

question: What does the concept of informed choice mean in family planning?

options.A: Accepting whichever contraceptive method the clinic has in stock today
options.B: Selecting a method voluntarily after receiving balanced and complete facts
options.C: Allowing the attending physician to choose the safest method for the client
options.D: Following strict community traditions regarding family size and spacing

explanation: Informed choice requires that clients receive unbiased information and make their own voluntary decisions without pressure. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T1#BMP224_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a common oral medication used to treat uncomplicated yeast infections?

options.A: Azithromycin
options.B: Metronidazole
options.C: Penicillin V
options.D: Fluconazole

explanation: Fluconazole is a widely used oral antifungal drug that often clears yeast infections with a single dose in non-pregnant patients. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which professional group do midwives work most closely with in a tertiary maternity complex?

options.A: Agricultural extension officers
options.B: Financial accountants
options.C: Obstetrician-gynecologists
options.D: Civil engineers

explanation: Midwives in tertiary maternity complexes collaborate directly with obstetrician-gynecologists to manage complex childbirth cases. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h4)

question: Where does the varicella-zoster virus hide in the body after the initial chickenpox infection heals?

options.A: In sensory nerve ganglia
options.B: In the red bone marrow
options.C: In the outer skin layers
options.D: In the muscle tissue

explanation: After chickenpox clears, the virus stays inactive inside nerve cell roots. It can sometimes reactivate later in life as shingles. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic behavioral sign of postpartum psychosis?

options.A: Steady weight gain and excessive sleep
options.B: Increased interest in household chores
options.C: Rapidly shifting mood and confusion
options.D: Prolonged periods of quiet meditation

explanation: Mothers with postpartum psychosis show very unstable moods and significant mental confusion. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T3#BMP223_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which condition is safe for a client using progestin-only pills?

options.A: Unexplained abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Controlled essential hypertension
options.C: Severe acute liver disease
options.D: Current active breast cancer

explanation: Unlike combined oral pills, progestin-only pills do not worsen high blood pressure, making them safe for women with controlled hypertension. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T5#BMP224_U3_T5_h3)

question: A new mother who was coping well begins to struggle after experiencing severe sleep deprivation and birth trauma. What does this show?

options.A: Mental health status is dynamic and influenced by life stressors
options.B: The mother had a hidden psychiatric illness before she got pregnant
options.C: Sleep deprivation only affects physical healing, never mental wellness
options.D: Midwives have no ability to influence a patient's mental state

explanation: Stressors like trauma and lack of sleep can shift a person along the continuum, proving that mental health changes in response to life events. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T1#BMP223_U1_T1_h3)

question: Who is the educational theorist most famous for popularizing the concept of andragogy?

options.A: Jean Piaget
options.B: Malcolm Knowles
options.C: Sigmund Freud
options.D: Ivan Pavlov

explanation: Malcolm Knowles established the core principles that define how adults learn and how instruction should be tailored for them. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T1#BMP312_U3_T1_h4)

question: What change happens inside heart muscle cells right after their blood supply is blocked?

options.A: They begin producing excess proteins to repair the cell wall.
options.B: They stop using glucose and rely entirely on stored body fat.
options.C: They increase their oxygen storage capacity to survive longer.
options.D: They switch from aerobic to anaerobic metabolism, producing lactic acid.

explanation: Without oxygen, cells cannot use normal energy pathways, leading to a buildup of acid that causes pain and damages cell membranes. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T4#BMP125_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does dropping out of school due to early pregnancy affect the long-term well-being of a young mother?

options.A: It guarantees she will receive financial support from the government
options.B: It gives her more time to focus entirely on learning traditional crafts
options.C: It improves her mental health by removing academic stress
options.D: It limits her future job prospects and keeps her trapped in poverty

explanation: Without a solid education or professional skills, finding stable, well-paying employment becomes extremely difficult, perpetuating financial hardship. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T2#BMP320_U3_T2_h5)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe throat pain, fever, swollen neck glands, and white spots on the tonsils, but no cough. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Viral bronchitis
options.B: Fungal stomatitis
options.C: Allergic rhinitis
options.D: Bacterial pharyngitis

explanation: The cluster of high fever, white spots on the tonsils, and lack of a cough points directly toward streptococcal bacterial pharyngitis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T4#BMP125_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does finger clubbing usually tell a healthcare worker about a patient's health status?

options.A: The person has accidentally injured their nail matrix with a heavy tool.
options.B: The patient has been suffering from a severe local fungal infection.
options.C: The individual lacks adequate dietary protein and vitamins.
options.D: The body has experienced long-term lack of sufficient oxygen.

explanation: Clubbing develops slowly over months or years in response to chronic low blood oxygen levels seen in certain heart and lung conditions. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T4#BMP110_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common emergency complication of advanced liver failure?

options.A: Rapid kidney failure known as hepatorenal syndrome
options.B: Massive bleeding from ruptured esophageal varices
options.C: Severe confusion and coma from hepatic encephalopathy
options.D: Sudden development of high blood pressure

explanation: Liver failure causes low blood pressure (hypotension) due to widespread vasodilation and fluid shifts, not high blood pressure. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T3#BMP125_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of providing good pain relief during labor for a patient with a heart condition?

options.A: To shorten the first stage of labor
options.B: To blunt the stress response and prevent blood pressure spikes
options.C: To prevent fetal distress caused by contractions
options.D: To eliminate the need for an intravenous line

explanation: Pain and anxiety release adrenaline, which raises heart rate and blood pressure and puts extra stress on a weak heart. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T4#BMP221_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which vital sign needs the closest monitoring after a patient receives a sedative medication?

options.A: Body temperature
options.B: Urine output
options.C: Capillary refill
options.D: Respiratory rate

explanation: Sedatives depress the central nervous system, making it essential to monitor breathing rate to catch dangerous slowing early. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h6)

question: How does progestin specifically block sperm from meeting an egg?

options.A: By raising the core body temperature of the uterus
options.B: By opening the fallopian tubes to flush them out
options.C: By destroying sperm cells directly in the vagina
options.D: By making the cervical mucus thick and impenetrable

explanation: Progestin alters the consistency of cervical mucus, creating a thick barrier that stops sperm from swimming upward into the womb. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why should a midwife keep vaginal examinations to a minimum during a home birth?

options.A: To preserve sterile gloves and equipment in the kit
options.B: To ensure the progress of labor follows a strict timeline
options.C: To reduce the risk of bringing bacteria into the birth canal
options.D: To prevent unnecessary discomfort and anxiety for the mother

explanation: Each vaginal examination increases the likelihood of ascending infection and subsequent puerperal sepsis. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T3#BMP215_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is an important nursing duty when caring for a postpartum patient taking antipsychotic medications?

options.A: Encouraging the mother to run daily marathons to burn off drug energy
options.B: Stopping the medication as soon as the patient smiles once
options.C: Monitoring for adverse side effects and checking vital signs regularly
options.D: Withholding all fluids to prevent drug dilution in the bloodstream

explanation: Antipsychotics can cause side effects like drowsiness and blood pressure changes that need close monitoring. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T3#BMP223_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do untreated reproductive tract infections contribute to spontaneous preterm birth?

options.A: Inflammatory chemicals trigger early uterine contractions and weaken the fetal membranes
options.B: They directly cause the placenta to grow too large for the uterine cavity
options.C: They force the mother's body to stop producing progesterone permanently
options.D: They block the umbilical cord and cut off oxygen supply to the fetus

explanation: Infection releases prostaglandins and inflammatory cytokines that stimulate the uterus to contract and cause membranes to rupture prematurely. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is an important safety rule when holding a medication tube near a newborn's eye?

options.A: Always warm the metal tip in warm water first
options.B: Press the tip firmly against the lower eyelid

question: Why do insulin requirements drop dramatically right after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: Breastfeeding instantly cures both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes
options.B: The baby's pancreas starts supplying insulin to the mother
options.C: Placental hormones that cause insulin resistance are suddenly removed
options.D: The mother stops eating for several days following childbirth

explanation: The placenta produces hormones that resist insulin; once delivered, insulin sensitivity returns quickly, lowering the required dose. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T3#BMP221_U4_T3_h8)

question: At what stage of life is the HPV vaccine most effective when given to girls?

options.A: After they have been diagnosed with cancer
options.B: After reaching menopause
options.C: During their third trimester of pregnancy
options.D: Before their first sexual encounter

explanation: The vaccine works best when given before any exposure to the human papillomavirus through sexual activity. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h4)

question: What are the two most common vasomotor symptoms experienced during menopause?

options.A: Joint pain and morning stiffness
options.B: Hot flashes and night sweats
options.C: Weight gain and hair thinning
options.D: Mood swings and anxiety spells

explanation: Hot flashes and night sweats are the classic signs of vasomotor instability during the menopausal transition. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T2#BMP320_U1_T2_h1)
